column2: HEA-001: The platform MUST maintain approved, versioned red-flag rule packs by age group and pregnancy status. Rule execution precedes the LLM respons
HEA-002: A red flag MUST create an immutable risk event, urgent case, recommended action, configured destination and escalation timer.
HEA-003: The LLM MUST NOT downgrade a deterministic urgent classification. Only an authorised clinician can override it, with reason and audit.
HEA-004: When location or referral data is unavailable, the system MUST state that limitation and give the nationally approved fallback instruction.
HEA-005: The response MUST use action-first language: what to do now, what not to delay, where to seek help and what information to take.

AGR-002: The system MUST distinguish observation from confirmed diagnosis. Visual classification outputs are “possible matches” until evidence and con

AGR-004: Advice SHOULD prioritise feasible, low-cost integrated pest-management actions and explicitly flag actions that could harm people, animals, c
AGR-005: Market prices MUST display source, market, unit, grade/quality where known, observation timestamp and staleness. The assistant must never rep
EDU-001: The platform MUST store an age/grade band and preferred language, not infer sensitive traits from voice.
EDU-002: Adaptation MUST use demonstrated mastery, requested difficulty, response history and educator configuration. It MUST NOT label a child as uni
EDU-003: The tutor MUST use a “teach, check, adapt” loop: explain one concept, ask a short comprehension check, assess the answer against a rubric, th

EDU-005: Child-facing conversations MUST apply age-appropriate content filters, privacy minimisation, abuse/self-harm escalation and restrictions on c
IAM-001: Citizens MAY use anonymous or pseudonymous sessions where service policy permits. Phone verification cannot be the only access route.
IAM-002: Staff use federated identity where available, MFA and role plus attribute-based access.
IAM-003: Sensitive exports, clinical overrides, rule publication and break-glass access require step-up authentication.
IAM-004: Break-glass access expires automatically, requires justification and alerts the data protection/safety owner.
IAM-005: Role changes revoke active sessions and queued export links according to policy.
CON-001: Consent is purpose-specific: service delivery, follow-up contact, precise location, analytics, research/model improvement and cross-programme
CON-002: Consent scripts are delivered in the selected language and channel and record script version plus affirmative action.
CON-003: Withdrawal stops future optional processing but preserves records required by lawful retention; the user receives a plain-language explanatio
CON-004: Proxy/caregiver relationships record who is present, on whose behalf and the authority/assent basis.
CAS-001: Queues support domain, geography, service point, risk, skill, language and workload routing.
CAS-002: Assignment is atomic and prevents two workers unknowingly owning the same case.
CAS-003: Notes support structured fields and append-only narrative entries; edits create new versions.
CAS-004: SLA timers pause only for configured reasons and every pause is audited.
CAS-005: Merge and duplicate resolution preserve all source identifiers and events.
CAS-006: Closure requires outcome, action taken, citizen reachability and follow-up decision.
NOT-001: Templates are versioned by language, channel, domain, risk and sensitivity.
NOT-002: Delivery attempts, provider IDs, consent, quiet hours, failures and retries are recorded.
NOT-003: Urgent alerts use an escalation policy with acknowledgement; a sent message is not treated as acknowledged.
NOT-004: Lock-screen/SMS text uses privacy-safe wording.
NOT-005: Broadcasts require audience estimate, duplicate suppression, approval, rate controls and opt-out compliance.
